The '''X-23 StarWorker''' was an intra-system [[space barge]] produced by the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] manufacturing corporation [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]]. It was capable of carrying up to 5,000 [[Metric ton/Legends|metric tons]] of cargo in its 2,000 [[Cubic meter/Legends|cubic meter]] bay.

==Characteristics==
Bereft of weapons, [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|339|X-23 StarWorker}}</ref> and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]],<ref name="SWS" /> the 38-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] long StarWorker<ref name="CSWE" /> had [[Foodstuff/Legends|consumables]] enough to last a [[Standard week/Legends|week]],<ref name="SWS" /> and could be crewed by only two [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] with a [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]] [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droid]].<ref name="CSWE" />

==History==
In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] flew a StarWorker to the [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] [[Jedi Praxeum]] to offload supplies.<ref name="DA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The X-23 StarWorker was created by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]] for ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' published in [[1987]]. The stat block and description in the first edition of ''The Star Wars Sourcebook'' states the Starworker doesn't have a hyperdrive, however the stat block lists a NavComputer (for no use). This oddity repeats in further RPG sources. Its first appearance was in ''[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|Dark Apprentice]]'', in [[1994]]. In that book, [[Kevin J. Anderson]] has Wedge Antilles delivering cargo from Coruscant to Yavin IV in a StarWorker, despite the starship being an "intra-system" vessel lacking a [[hyperdrive]].

[[File:X-23spacebarge-piratesprivateers.jpg|thumb|right|180px|''X-23'' picture in ''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''.]]
''[[Pirates & Privateers]]'' uses a different picture for the X-23. This seems to be an error, as it looks like an unknown [[space barge]] that appears in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' near the X-23 description (the StarWorker has its own picture, however).
